name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q01 - Livestock productivity and farm management

questiontext.text:
Read the following three statements regarding animal husbandry and farm management:

Statement I: More than 70 per cent of the world livestock population is in India and China, yet their contribution to the world farm produce is only 25 per cent.

Statement II: In dairy farm management, milk yield is primarily dependent on the quality of breeds having high yielding potential and resistance to diseases under local climatic conditions.

Statement III: Poultry refers to the class of domesticated fowl used for food or for their eggs, typically including chicken and ducks, and sometimes turkey and geese.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal husbandry encompasses the scientific care, breeding, and management of livestock, including dairying and poultry farming, to enhance both the quality and quantity of animal produce.

Step 2: Evaluation of Global Livestock Productivity
India and China together account for more than 70 per cent of the world's livestock population, but their contribution to global farm produce is only about 25 per cent, indicating very low productivity per unit and the need for modern breeding and management technologies. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Dairy Farm Management
Milk yield in a dairy farm depends primarily on the quality of breeds selected for high yielding potential under local climatic conditions combined with disease resistance, along with proper housing, scientific feeding, and stringent hygiene. Thus, the second claim is true.

Step 4: Evaluation of Poultry Farming
Poultry comprises domesticated fowl (birds) reared for meat or eggs, typically including chicken and ducks, and sometimes turkey and geese. Thus, the third claim is also true.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
All three claims regarding livestock productivity, dairy breed selection, and poultry definition are scientifically accurate.

answer.text: All three statements are correct.
Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q02 - Apiculture and freshwater versus marine fisheries

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding apiculture and fisheries:

Statement I: Keeping beehives in crop fields during the flowering period of sunflower, Brassica, apple, and pear increases pollination efficiency and improves both crop yield and honey yield.

Statement II: Beeswax produced by honeybees finds extensive industrial use in the preparation of cosmetics and polishes of various kinds.

Statement III: Hilsa, Sardines, and Mackerel are very common freshwater fishes eaten in India.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Apiculture (bee-keeping) provides honey, beeswax, and vital pollination services for agricultural crops, while fisheries supply aquatic food from both freshwater and marine habitats.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pollination and Beeswax
Honeybees act as pollinators for many crop species such as sunflower, Brassica, apple, and pear; placing beehives in crop fields during flowering enhances pollination efficiency, boosting both crop and honey yields. Additionally, beeswax is widely used in industry to make cosmetics and polishes. Therefore, the first two claims are true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Fish Habitats
Common freshwater fishes include Catla, Rohu, and common carp, whereas Hilsa, Sardines, Mackerel, and Pomfrets are marine fishes. Classifying Hilsa, Sardines, and Mackerel as freshwater fishes is therefore incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Only the first two claims regarding bee pollination and beeswax utility are correct, while the habitat classification of marine fishes is false.

answer.text: All three statements are correct.
Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
Only Statement I is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q03 - Inbreeding out-crossing and cross-breeding in animals

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following three statements on animal breeding methods:

Statement I: Continued inbreeding for 4–6 generations decreases homozygosity and prevents the evolution of a pureline in animals.

Statement II: Out-crossing involves mating animals within the same breed that have no common ancestors on either side of their pedigree up to 4–6 generations, and a single outcross often helps overcome inbreeding depression.

Statement III: Hisardale is a new breed of sheep developed in Punjab by crossing Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal breeding strategies manipulate genetic relatedness—either through inbreeding within closely related individuals or out-breeding between unrelated individuals—to fix desirable traits or restore vigour.

Step 2: Evaluation of Inbreeding Effects
Inbreeding refers to the mating of closely related individuals within the same breed for 4–6 generations. It increases homozygosity rather than decreasing it, which is essential for evolving a pureline in any animal and exposing harmful recessive genes for elimination by selection. Hence, the claim that inbreeding decreases homozygosity is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Out-crossing and Cross-breeding
Out-crossing is the mating of animals within the same breed with no common ancestors on either side of their pedigree for 4–6 generations; a single outcross frequently restores fertility and yield lost due to inbreeding depression. Furthermore, cross-breeding mates superior males of one breed with superior females of another breed, exemplified by Hisardale, a sheep breed developed in Punjab by crossing Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams. Both of these claims are true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding out-crossing overcoming inbreeding depression and the cross-bred origin of Hisardale sheep are correct, whereas the claim about inbreeding decreasing homozygosity is incorrect.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
All three statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q04 - Multiple ovulation embryo transfer and interspecific hybridisation

questiontext.text:
Read the following three statements about controlled breeding technologies:

Statement I: In Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET), a cow is administered hormones with FSH-like activity to induce follicular maturation and super ovulation, producing 6–8 eggs per cycle.

Statement II: In MOET, the fertilised eggs at 8–32 cells stages are recovered surgically and transferred back into the genetic mother.

Statement III: The mule is an economically valuable progeny produced by interspecific hybridisation between male and female animals of two different related species.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Controlled breeding programmes such as MOET and interspecific hybridisation improve herd quality and combine desirable traits across species.

Step 2: Evaluation of Hormonal Induction in MOET
In MOET, a cow is given hormones with FSH-like activity to stimulate follicular maturation and super ovulation so that she yields 6–8 eggs instead of the usual single egg per cycle. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Embryo Recovery and Transfer in MOET
After mating with an elite bull or artificial insemination, the fertilised eggs at the 8–32 cells stages are recovered non-surgically (not surgically) and transferred to surrogate mothers (not the genetic mother), leaving the genetic mother free for another round of super ovulation. Hence, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Evaluation of Interspecific Hybridisation
Interspecific hybridisation involves mating male and female animals of two different related species, and the mule is a classic example combining desirable features of both parents. Thus, the third claim is true.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims describing FSH-like hormonal super ovulation in MOET and interspecific hybridisation producing the mule are correct, while the claim regarding surgical recovery and re-implantation into the genetic mother is incorrect.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
All three statements are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q05 - Steps in plant breeding programmes

questiontext.text:
Examine the following three statements regarding the main steps in breeding a new genetic variety of a crop:

Statement I: The entire collection of plants or seeds having all the diverse alleles for all genes in a given crop is called germplasm collection.

Statement II: Cross hybridisation among selected parents guarantees that almost every cross will combine the desired characters into a single hybrid plant.

Statement III: Before release, newly selected lines are tested in farmers' fields for one growing season at a single representative location.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Systematic plant breeding proceeds through five sequential stages: collection of variability, evaluation and selection of parents, cross hybridisation, selection of superior recombinants, and multi-location testing before release.

Step 2: Evaluation of Germplasm Collection
Genetic variability is the root of any breeding programme, and the entire collection of plants or seeds possessing all diverse alleles for all genes in a given crop is defined as the germplasm collection. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cross Hybridisation Efficiency
Cross hybridisation is tedious and time-consuming, and hybrids do not necessarily combine the desired traits; typically only one in a few hundred to a thousand crosses exhibits the desired combination. Therefore, claiming that almost every cross succeeds is false.

Step 4: Evaluation of Testing and Release
After evaluation in research fields, newly selected lines must be tested in farmers' fields for at least three growing seasons at several locations across all agroclimatic zones where the crop is grown, compared against a local check cultivar. Testing for only one season at a single location is therefore false.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the definition of germplasm collection is correct, whereas the claims regarding cross hybridisation success rate and single-season testing are incorrect.

answer.text: Only Statement I is correct.
Only Statement II is correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q06 - Green revolution wheat rice and sugarcane varieties

questiontext.text:
Read the following three statements about high-yielding crop varieties developed for the Green Revolution in India:

Statement I: Sonalika and Kalyan Sona are high-yielding, disease-resistant semi-dwarf varieties of rice introduced in India in 1963.

Statement II: Better-yielding semi-dwarf rice varieties Jaya and Ratna were developed in India, following derivatives from IR-8 and Taichung Native-1.

Statement III: Saccharum barberi, originally grown in north India, had thicker stems and higher sugar content than the tropical cane Saccharum officinarum.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Green Revolution in India relied on semi-dwarf wheat and rice varieties as well as interspecific sugarcane hybrids combining regional adaptability with high yield.

Step 2: Evaluation of Wheat Varieties
Sonalika and Kalyan Sona introduced in 1963 are high-yielding and disease-resistant semi-dwarf varieties of wheat, not rice. Therefore, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Rice Varieties
Semi-dwarf rice derivatives from IR-8 (developed at IRRI, Philippines) and Taichung Native-1 (from Taiwan) were introduced in 1966, and later better-yielding semi-dwarf rice varieties Jaya and Ratna were developed in India. Thus, the second claim is true.

Step 4: Evaluation of Sugarcane Species
Saccharum barberi grown in north India had poor sugar content and yield, whereas tropical Saccharum officinarum grown in south India had thicker stems and higher sugar content but did not grow well in north India. Reversing these traits makes the third claim false.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the claim describing the Indian semi-dwarf rice varieties Jaya and Ratna is correct.

answer.text: Only Statement I is correct.
Only Statement II is correct.
Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q07 - Plant breeding for disease resistance

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding disease-resistant crop varieties:

Statement I: Himgiri is a disease-resistant variety of Brassica bred for resistance against white rust.

Statement II: Pusa Komal is a variety of chilli resistant to tobacco mosaic virus and leaf curl.

Statement III: Resistance to yellow mosaic virus in bhindi (Abelmoschus esculentus) was transferred from a wild species, resulting in the variety Parbhani kranti.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Breeding for disease resistance uses conventional hybridisation and selection or wild-relative gene transfer to protect crops from fungal, bacterial, and viral pathogens.

Step 2: Evaluation of Himgiri and Pusa Komal
Himgiri is a variety of wheat resistant to leaf and stripe rust and hill bunt, whereas Pusa swarnim (Karan rai) is the Brassica variety resistant to white rust. Similarly, Pusa Komal is a cowpea variety resistant to bacterial blight, whereas Pusa Sadabahar is the chilli variety resistant to chilli mosaic virus, tobacco mosaic virus, and leaf curl. Thus, both the first and second claims are false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Parbhani kranti
Resistance to yellow mosaic virus in bhindi (Abelmoschus esculentus) was successfully transferred from a related wild species via sexual hybridisation, yielding the resistant variety Parbhani kranti. Thus, the third claim is true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Only the claim describing the transfer of yellow mosaic virus resistance in bhindi to produce Parbhani kranti is correct.

answer.text: Only Statement I is correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.
Only Statement III is correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q08 - Morphological and biochemical traits for insect resistance

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following three statements regarding plant breeding for insect pest resistance:

Statement I: Smooth-leaved and nectar-rich cotton varieties do not attract bollworms.

Statement II: Low aspartic acid, high nitrogen, and high sugar content in maize lead to resistance against maize stem borers.

Statement III: Pusa Gaurav is a variety of okra (bhindi) bred for resistance against shoot and fruit borer.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Insect pest resistance in crop plants arises from specific morphological, biochemical, or physiological traits, and resistant cultivars have been released through hybridisation and selection.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cotton and Maize Resistance Traits
In cotton, smooth-leaved and nectar-less (not nectar-rich) varieties fail to attract bollworms. In maize, resistance to maize stem borers is conferred by high aspartic acid, low nitrogen, and low sugar content, which is the exact opposite of the second claim. Hence, both the first and second claims are false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Pusa Gaurav
Pusa Gaurav is a variety of Brassica (rapeseed mustard) resistant to aphids, whereas Pusa Sawani and Pusa A-4 are the okra (bhindi) varieties resistant to shoot and fruit borer. Therefore, the third claim is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
None of the three claims accurately reflects the morphological traits, biochemical composition, or released varieties for insect pest resistance.

answer.text: Only Statement I is correct.
Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statement III is correct.
None of the statements is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q09 - Biofortification and nutrient enriched crops

questiontext.text:
Read the following three statements regarding biofortification for improved food quality:

Statement I: Biofortification involves breeding crops with higher levels of vitamins and minerals, or higher protein and healthier fats, to combat micronutrient deficiencies known as hidden hunger.

Statement II: The high-protein wheat variety Atlas 66 has been used as a donor to improve cultivated wheat, and maize hybrids developed in 2000 contained twice the amount of lysine and tryptophan compared to existing hybrids.

Statement III: The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi has released vitamin A enriched bitter gourd and tomato, and vitamin C enriched carrots and spinach.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biofortification is the most practical strategy to improve public health by breeding crops enriched in proteins, healthier fats, vitamins, and essential micronutrients such as iron, vitamin A, iodine, and zinc.

Step 2: Evaluation of Biofortification Objectives and Cereals
Breeding crops with elevated vitamins, minerals, protein, and healthier fats directly addresses hidden hunger, which affects three billion people worldwide. In cereals, maize hybrids developed in 2000 doubled the levels of amino acids lysine and tryptophan, and the high-protein wheat variety Atlas 66 served as a donor for improving cultivated wheat. Thus, the first two claims are true.

Step 3: Evaluation of IARI Biofortified Vegetables
IARI, New Delhi released vitamin A enriched carrots, spinach, and pumpkin, whereas vitamin C enriched varieties were bitter gourd, bathua, mustard, and tomato (along with iron and calcium enriched spinach and bathua). Swapping the vitamin A and vitamin C crop groups makes the third claim false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Only the claims covering the definition of biofortification and the biofortified wheat and maize examples are correct, while the IARI vegetable vitamin pairings are reversed.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.
All three statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q10 - Single cell protein sources and biomass production

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding Single Cell Protein (SCP):

Statement I: A shift from grain to meat diets increases the demand for cereals because producing 1 kg of meat by animal farming requires 3–10 kg of grain.

Statement II: The blue-green alga Spirulina can be grown easily on waste water from potato processing plants, straw, molasses, animal manure, and sewage, providing nutrient-rich food while reducing environmental pollution.

Statement III: Because of its high rate of biomass production and growth, the bacterium Methylophilus methylotrophus can be expected to produce 25 tonnes of protein.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Single Cell Protein (SCP) uses microbes grown on an industrial scale as an alternative, efficient source of protein for human and animal nutrition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Trophic Grain Demand
Animal farming is trophically inefficient compared to direct grain consumption; it takes 3–10 kg of grain to produce 1 kg of meat, so shifting toward meat diets raises cereal demand. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Spirulina Cultivation
Spirulina, a blue-green alga, grows readily on starch-rich waste water from potato processing plants, straw, molasses, animal manure, and even sewage, yielding food rich in protein, minerals, fats, carbohydrates, and vitamins while simultaneously mitigating environmental pollution. Thus, the second claim is true.

Step 4: Evaluation of Methylophilus methylotrophus
Due to its exceptionally high rate of biomass production and growth, the bacterium Methylophilus methylotrophus can be expected to produce 25 tonnes of protein. Thus, the third claim is also true.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
All three claims accurately describe the rationale, substrates, pollution-reduction benefits, and microbial productivity of Single Cell Protein.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
All three statements are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q11 - Totipotency micropropagation meristem culture and somatic hybridisation

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following three statements on plant tissue culture techniques:

Statement I: Totipotency is the capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell or explant grown in a sterile nutrient medium containing a carbon source such as sucrose, inorganic salts, vitamins, amino acids, and growth regulators like auxins and cytokinins.

Statement II: Plants produced in thousands through micro-propagation are genetically different from the original plant and are termed somatic hybrids.

Statement III: Even when a plant is infected with a virus, its apical and axillary meristems remain free of virus and can be cultured in vitro to obtain virus-free plants, while somatic hybridisation fuses naked protoplasts of two different varieties as demonstrated in pomato.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant tissue culture exploits cellular totipotency under sterile in vitro conditions for rapid clonal multiplication, virus elimination, and protoplast fusion.

Step 2: Evaluation of Totipotency and Nutrient Medium
Any plant cell or explant can regenerate into a whole plant—a property called totipotency—when cultured in a sterile nutrient medium supplying sucrose (carbon source), inorganic salts, vitamins, amino acids, and growth regulators such as auxins and cytokinins. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Micro-propagation and Somaclones
Thousands of plants generated by micro-propagation are genetically identical to the original parent plant and are called somaclones, not genetically different somatic hybrids. Therefore, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Evaluation of Meristem Culture and Somatic Hybridisation
Apical and axillary meristems of virus-infected plants are free of virus and can be cultured in vitro to recover virus-free plants (such as banana, sugarcane, and potato). Separately, somatic hybridisation digests cell walls to isolate naked protoplasts from two different varieties and fuses them to form somatic hybrids, such as pomato from tomato and potato protoplasts. Thus, the third claim is true.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding totipotency with its nutrient requirements and meristem culture alongside somatic hybridisation are correct, whereas the claim misidentifying somaclones as genetically different somatic hybrids is incorrect.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.
All three statements are correct.
